text:
Yegor Sharangovich scored Calgary's only goal in an overtime loss in Seattle on Nov. 4, his third of the season. It's been that kind of year: 5 points in 17 games, and he played just 11:18 in Friday's loss to Anaheim, his lowest of the season.

The good news is in the shot share. The Flames take 56% of the shot attempts with him on the ice at five on five and are more than five points better in expected goals (the quality of chances) with him than without. Calgary has scored 5.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there, which has cost him points. His own finishing, 3 goals on 4.08 expected, is a little behind too.

He has a heavy shot (88th percentile) and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season had 71% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season, which tempers how much we'd expect. We project about 17 goals. Watch his minutes: a 28-year-old with this profile shouldn't be sliding down a lineup that's missing Connor Zary and Brennan Othmann.
headline: Sharangovich's quiet November
